note.text:
Mixture or compound?
• Make-up: a mixture's parts can be in any amounts; a compound's elements are in a fixed ratio.
• Properties: in a mixture each part keeps its properties; a compound has new properties.
• Separation: a mixture can be separated by physical methods; a compound only by a chemical reaction.
• Melting and boiling: a mixture melts or boils over a range; a compound at fixed temperatures.
• Making it: mixing usually gives no heat or light; forming a compound often gives out (or takes in) heat.
Example: iron filings and sulfur mixed together are a mixture (a magnet pulls out the iron); heated together they react to form iron sulfide, a compound (a magnet no longer pulls it).

worked_example.problem: Iron filings and sulfur powder are mixed, then the mixture is heated strongly until it glows. What do you have before and after heating?
steps: Before: a magnet pulls out the iron; the yellow sulfur stays. It is a mixture.
Heating: the mixture glows: a chemical reaction gives out heat.
After: a black solid, iron sulfide; a magnet does not pull it. It is a compound.
worked_example.answer: Before: a mixture. After: a compound (iron sulfide).

cards.idea: A mixture can be separated by physical methods; a compound needs a chemical reaction.
example: Salt water: evaporate. Water itself: only a reaction splits it.

cards.idea: In a mixture each part keeps its properties; a compound has new properties.
example: Iron + sulfur mixed: a magnet still pulls the iron. Iron sulfide: it does not.

cards.idea: A compound has a fixed make-up and fixed melting and boiling points; a mixture does not.
example: Water is always H₂O and boils at {b} °C (pure, normal pressure).

check.prompt: Which is true of a compound?

right.text: Its elements are always in the same fixed ratio.

wrong.text: Its parts can be in any amounts.
It can be separated with a magnet or a filter.
Each part keeps its own properties.

questions.prompt: Is {x.t} a mixture or a compound?

misconceptions.explain: Ask: are the parts chemically joined in a fixed ratio?

questions.prompt: Iron and sulfur have been heated together. How can you show that a compound has formed?

right.text: A magnet no longer pulls out the iron.

wrong.text: The mixture is still yellow and grey.
wrong.explain: Those are the old properties: a compound has new ones.

wrong.text: You can still pick out the sulfur.
wrong.explain: If you can, it is still a mixture.
Weighing does not show whether the elements have joined.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: A compound has a fixed composition.
A mixture can be separated by physical methods.
Forming a compound often gives out heat.

wrong.text: Water can be separated into hydrogen and oxygen by filtering.
wrong.explain: Water is a compound: only a chemical reaction splits it.

wrong.text: In a compound, each element keeps its own properties.
wrong.explain: A compound has new properties; each part keeps its properties only in a mixture.
